sources.title: What's A Startup? First Principles.
sources.author: Steve Blank
sources.reliability: Authoritative for the author's customer-development definition; practitioner proposition, not a universal empirical law.
sources.notes: Read article body, excluding comments. Search for a repeatable business model is distinct from execution. No fixed age, funding or headcount stage rule inferred.
supported_claims: Startup work tests business-model hypotheses
Models may change repeatedly as observed behavior contradicts assumptions

sources.title: The Lean Startup: Methodology
sources.author: Eric Ries / The Lean Startup
sources.reliability: Official method description; not independent causal evaluation.
sources.notes: Publication year is not displayed. The 2011 book was not read in full. Validated learning and Build-Measure-Learn are the sourced concepts.
supported_claims: Validated learning is progress under uncertainty
Experiments inform pivot or persevere decisions
Actionable measurement is preferable to output counts
not_supported: Every MVP is a software release
Every experiment must be an A/B test

sources.title: The Business Model Canvas
sources.author: Strategyzer; Alexander Osterwalder and Yves Pigneur (framework origin)
sources.reliability: Framework creator's official page; commercial publisher; canvas is a modeling tool, not validation evidence.
sources.notes: Current public landing page read; subscription playbooks and linked book not accessed. Nine interconnected blocks describe one business model.
supported_claims: Canvas models how value is created, delivered and captured
Model blocks are interdependent
Canvas versions should change with evidence

sources.title: Validate your ideas with The Test Card
sources.author: Alexander Osterwalder
sources.reliability: Authoritative account of tool fields; no universal success threshold provided.
sources.notes: Article text read; embedded video not watched. Hypothesis, test, metric and success threshold are specified before learning.
supported_claims: Specify hypothesis, experiment, measurement and threshold explicitly

sources.title: Capture (customer) insights and actions with The Learning Card
sources.author: Nabila Amarsy
sources.reliability: Official companion tool explanation; practitioner guidance.
sources.notes: Text read; video not watched. Observations must be distinguished from interpretation and subsequent action.
supported_claims: Link tested assumptions, observations, insights and actions

sources.title: YC's Essential Startup Advice
sources.author: Geoff Ralston / Y Combinator
sources.reliability: Experienced accelerator guidance; portfolio selection and survivorship limit generalization.
sources.notes: Read body and references list; linked articles not all reviewed. Launch advice requires adaptation to regulated, safety-critical and capital-intensive contexts.
supported_claims: Learning can begin through manual customer service
Growth before customer value and sustainable unit economics can consume cash
Funding valuation is not operating validation

sources.title: The Real Product Market Fit
sources.author: Michael Seibel
sources.reliability: Qualitative practitioner interpretation; venture-scale orientation, not a calibrated diagnostic test.
sources.notes: Article body read. Demand from satisfied loyal customers matters more than headcount or financing. Does not establish a universal numeric PMF cut-off.
supported_claims: Avoid confusing funding and employee count with PMF
Premature expansion increases burn before demand is understood

sources.title: Disciplined entrepreneurship: 6 questions for startup success
sources.author: Bill Aulet / MIT Sloan
sources.reliability: Authoritative condensed method excerpt; not full book or independent efficacy study.
sources.notes: Public edited excerpt read. Context is innovation-driven entrepreneurship. Focused beachhead, buying process, pricing and economics are relevant; the original 24 steps are not reproduced here.
supported_claims: Select a focused initial customer segment
Understand decision makers and purchasing process
Test pricing and identify key assumptions before expansion

sources.title: Jobs to Be Done Theory
sources.author: Clayton Christensen Institute
sources.reliability: Authoritative theory explanation with illustrative cases; cases do not prove all applications.
sources.notes: Definition and explainer read. Jobs describe desired progress in circumstances, including functional, emotional and social aspects. No copyrighted case narrative copied.
supported_claims: Customer choices depend on desired progress and circumstances
Demographics alone may conceal motivations
